B13C127.summary: A run of short teachings, each given by a different sage or deity, on ritual conduct: offerings on lunar days, household objects and habits that drive away the gods and ancestors, and rules of hospitality. The last teaching, from Jamadagni, says a pure heart counts for more than costly sacrifice. The section treats ritual merit as depending on both correct practice and inner purity.

scenes.B13C127S01: A string of teachings from Vibhavasu, Sree, Angiras, Gargya and Dhaumya on offerings, the household items that displease the gods, and the duties that bring merit.
scenes.B13C127S02: Jamadagni teaches that an impure heart undoes even great sacrifices, while a pure heart is worth as much as them.

shots.B13C127S01H01: Vibhavasu (Surya) describes two offerings to the sun on full-moon days and warns that cutting trees or using a tooth-stick on new-moon days brings sin and angers the ancestors.
shots.B13C127S01H02: Sree says a house with scattered vessels and beaten women drives the gods and ancestors away, so they refuse its offerings.
shots.B13C127S01H03: Angiras says a man's offspring multiply if he stands under a Karanja tree every night for a year with a lamp and Suvarchala roots in his hand.
shots.B13C127S01H04: Gargya lists duties such as hospitality, lamps at sacrifice halls, no daytime sleep, no meat, and no harm to cows and Brahmanas, and says the gods reject Sraddha offerings when impure women are near.
shots.B13C127S01H05: Dhaumya says broken pots and beds, roosters, dogs and trees growing inside the house are inauspicious, so no tree should be planted at home.
shots.B13C127S02H01: Jamadagni says a man with an impure heart goes to hell even after grand sacrifices, and a poor Brahmana's small gift of barley with a pure heart earned him Brahman's realm.

B13C128.summary: Vayu gives duties for the four rainy months and for ancestral rites, and names faults that bring sin, such as letting a Sudra kindle the sacred fire or letting unqualified women take part in rites. He gives an expiation of three days of fasting and fire offerings made with a mixture of cow's urine, dung, milk and ghee. He ends by saying that those who avoid these faults or expiate them reach heaven.

scenes.B13C128S01: Vayu's rainy-season duties, the sins of improper ritual helpers, and the three-day expiation that restores the sinner's standing.

shots.B13C128S01H01: Vayu lists rainy-season offerings to the ancestors and Brahmanas, names sins such as letting a Sudra light the fire or letting unfit women assist, gives a three-day expiation, and promises heaven to those who avoid or cleanse these faults.

B13C129.summary: Lomasa warns that men who seek other men's wives, have intercourse with barren women, or take what belongs to a Brahmana are cut off by their ancestors, and their offerings fail. He then praises gifts of ghee, Akshata, sesame-filled vessels, water, lamps and Krisara food on lunar days. He says these gifts earn great merit from the gods and ancestors, and that gifts of cows, land or an Agnishtoma sacrifice count as equal merit.

scenes.B13C129S01: Lomasa's warnings against adultery, barren women and theft from Brahmanas, followed by praise of gifts such as sesame vessels and lamps and the merit they bring.

shots.B13C129S01H01: Lomasa warns against adultery, sex with barren women and taking Brahmana property, then praises gifts of ghee, sesame, water, lamps and Krisara food and says what merit each brings.

B13C130.summary: The sages ask Arundhati, wife of Vasishtha, to reveal a high mystery of duty. She says it should be taught only to faithful or pure-hearted listeners, and describes washing a cow's horns and letting the water fall on one's head as bathing in all sacred waters. Brahman, Yama and Surya then speak in turn, praising gifts of water, lamps, Kapila cows, sandals and umbrellas and naming five kinds of sinners to avoid.

scenes.B13C130S01: Arundhati's teaching on the cow-horn rite, the praise of the gods, and the words of Brahman, Yama and Surya on charitable gifts and the five sinners to shun.

shots.B13C130S01H01: Bhishma says the sages ask Arundhati, wife of Vasishtha, to disclose a high mystery of duty.
shots.B13C130S01H02: Arundhati says the teaching should reach only faithful or pure-hearted listeners and describes the cow-horn rite; the gods and sages applaud her.
shots.B13C130S01H03: Brahman praises her teaching and grants that her penances will keep growing.
shots.B13C130S01H04: Yama relays Chitragupta's teachings on water, lamps, sandals, umbrellas and Kapila cows, and Surya then names five kinds of sinners to avoid.

B13C131.summary: The gods, ancestors and sages ask the Pramathas, night-wandering spirits, why they harm some men and what stops them. The Pramathas list unclean acts that leave men open to attack, such as neglecting purification after intercourse, insulting elders and spitting into water. They also name protections for a home, such as sacred marks, Akshata grain, a fire that never goes out, and certain animal skins, animals or sacrificial smoke.

scenes.B13C131S01: The Pramathas explain which conduct makes men vulnerable to them and which household practices keep them away.

shots.B13C131S01H01: Bhishma says the gods, ancestors and sages ask the Pramathas why they afflict some men and what acts protect against them.
shots.B13C131S01H02: The Pramathas name the unclean acts that make men easy prey and then list the protective marks, offerings, fires and household objects that keep them out.

B13C132.summary: Brahman sends the naga Renuka to ask the eight elephants that hold up the world about the mysteries of duty. The elephants prescribe Vali offerings of treacle and rice at an ant-hill on the eighth day of the dark fortnight in Karttika, saying the rite gives merit and eases their burden of holding up the earth. The gods, ancestors and sages applaud Renuka.

scenes.B13C132S01: Brahman sends Renuka to the elephants, who teach an ant-hill offering that brings merit and supports their work of holding up the earth.

shots.B13C132S01H01: Bhishma says the Grandsire Brahman names the naga Renuka and sends him to the mighty elephants that hold up the world.
shots.B13C132S01H02: Renuka asks the elephants to teach him the mysteries of religion and duty.
shots.B13C132S01H03: The elephants prescribe Vali offerings at an ant-hill with mantras, flowers, sugar, rice and cloth, describe their rewards, and the gods and sages applaud Renuka.

B13C133.summary: Maheswara closes this run of teachings by praising cows. He says feeding cows each day for a month while eating one meal a day brings great merit, and he notes the bull on his standard as a sign of his favour for them. Even one day's feeding of cows, he says, gives a fourth part of the merit of a person's good deeds in life, so cows should be worshipped by all.

scenes.B13C133S01: Maheswara teaches that feeding and worshipping cows brings great merit, and explains why he favours them.

shots.B13C133S01H01: Maheswara says a month of daily feeding of cows, with one meal a day for oneself, brings great merit, and mentions the bull on his standard as a sign of his favour for cows.

B13C134.summary: Skanda and Vishnu each teach a further duty and promise great rewards for hearing, reciting or performing it. Bhishma then says this knowledge is worth more than the whole earth. He adds that it must be withheld from the faithless, atheists, the unkind, and those who see other creatures as separate from themselves.

scenes.B13C134S01: Skanda's earth-and-honey rites, Vishnu's praise of hearing and reciting these teachings, and Bhishma's warning about whom to teach.

shots.B13C134S01H01: Skanda teaches two rites: smearing the body with earth from a blue bull's horns and bathing after three days, and offering honeyed food in a copper vessel to the full moon.
shots.B13C134S01H02: Vishnu says that daily hearing, reading or reciting these teachings keeps a person from evil and fear and brings merit.
shots.B13C134S01H03: Bhishma calls this knowledge more precious than the whole earth and says it must not be taught to the faithless, atheists, the unkind, and others he names.

B13C135.summary: Yudhishthira asks from whom each of the four classes may accept food. Bhishma says Brahmanas may eat with Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaisyas but never accept food from a Sudra, and he sets out the rules for the other classes. He names sources that defile, such as physicians, harlots and mechanics, and lists givers whose food must be refused, including killers of cows or Brahmanas and drunkards.

scenes.B13C135S01: Yudhishthira's question on eating rules, and Bhishma's answer on whose food each class may accept and whose it must refuse.

shots.B13C135S01H01: Yudhishthira asks from whom a Brahmana may accept food.
shots.B13C135S01H02: He adds the same question for a Kshatriya, a Vaisya and a Sudra.
shots.B13C135S01H03: He completes the question about the Vaisya and the Sudra.
shots.B13C135S01H04: Bhishma sets out which givers each class may take food from, and says that food from Sudras, physicians, harlots and others is defiling, while the duties of each class are briefly described.

B13C136.summary: Yudhishthira asks what expiation a Brahmana must make after accepting various foods and gifts, especially those used for the gods and ancestors. Bhishma gives a long list of purification rites, each tied to the kind of food or gift and the setting, such as funerals, eclipses and a dead person's house. He ends by saying that eating food partly eaten by another class is cleansed by smearing the body with auspicious substances.

scenes.B13C136S01: Yudhishthira's question about expiations, and Bhishma's list of purification rites for different foods, gifts and settings.

shots.B13C136S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what expiation a Brahmana must perform after accepting different foods, especially those offered to the gods and ancestors.
shots.B13C136S01H02: Bhishma lists expiations for accepting many foods and gifts and for eating in a dead person's house or with other classes, and ends with a rite for food partly eaten by another class.

B13C137.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether charity or devotion is the greater merit. Bhishma answers with a list of kings and sages who reached heaven through their gifts, teaching or penance, such as Sivi, Pratardana and Rantideva. He says their fame will last and that he will answer further doubts in the morning, as night has come.

scenes.B13C137S01: Yudhishthira asks which is better, charity or devotion, and Bhishma lists the royal and sage donors who gained heaven, then defers further answers to morning.

shots.B13C137S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which is better in this world, charity or devotion.
shots.B13C137S01H02: Bhishma names kings and sages, from Atreya and Sivi to Bhagiratha, who reached heaven through gifts, teaching or sacrifice, says their fame lasts, and promises to answer more questions in the morning.

B13C138.summary: Yudhishthira asks how many kinds of gift there are, what each brings, and to whom each should be given. Bhishma answers that gifts are made for five motives: a wish for merit, a wish for profit, fear, free choice, and pity. He gives an example for each and says gifts raise the giver's merit and fame, and that Brahman advised giving according to one's power.

scenes.B13C138S01: Yudhishthira's questions about kinds of gift, and Bhishma's classification of gifts by motive.

shots.B13C138S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how many kinds of gift there are, what fruits each brings, and to whom each should be made.
shots.B13C138S01H02: Bhishma names five motives for giving, illustrates each with a short example, and says gifts increase merit and fame.

B13C139.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to teach on religion and profit, and Bhishma agrees to tell of Vishnu's power and a doubt that troubled Rudra and his spouse. He describes how Krishna, during a long vow, received sages at his hermitage, where fire from his mouth burned a mountain and then was called back and the mountain restored. When the sages ask about it, Krishna says the fire is his own energy and asks them to tell him something wonderful, and they choose Narada to recount a story.

scenes.B13C139S01: Yudhishthira's request, Bhishma's opening, and Krishna's vow-time episode in which fire from his mouth burns and then restores a mountain, followed by his explanation to the sages.
scenes.B13C139S02: The ascetics ask Narada to tell the story of the Himavat wonder, and he begins.

shots.B13C139S01H01: Yudhishthira praises Bhishma's learning and asks him to teach on religion and profit, since no one else can now serve as their teacher.
shots.B13C139S01H02: The narrator, Vaisampayana, says Bhishma, moved by affection for the king, prepares to answer.
shots.B13C139S01H03: Bhishma promises tales of Vishnu's power and of a doubt that troubled Rudra and his spouse, and describes Krishna's long vow, when sages came and a fire from his mouth burned a mountain and was then restored.
shots.B13C139S01H04: The sages praise Krishna as creator and destroyer and ask him to explain the fire.
shots.B13C139S01H05: Krishna says the fire is his own energy from a penance for a son equal to him, and asks the sages to tell him something wonderful they have heard.
shots.B13C139S02H01: The sages ask Narada to relate the wonder they saw on the Himavat mountains, and he begins his story.

B13C140.summary: Narada tells of Shiva (Mahadeva) resting on the Himavat mountains, surrounded by gods, ghostly beings and sages. Uma playfully covers his eyes, plunging the world into darkness, and a third eye then opens on his forehead and burns the mountain until Shiva restores it at her plea. Uma asks why he has the third eye, why he burned and restored the mountain, and why his faces, hair and throat look as they do. Shiva agrees to explain.

scenes.B13C140S01: Narada describes Shiva's retreat on the Himavat, Uma covering his eyes, the third eye that burns the mountain, and Uma's questions about his form and actions.
scenes.B13C140S02: Shiva is pleased and agrees to explain the reasons for his forms.

shots.B13C140S01H01: Bhishma introduces Narada's account of a discourse between Sankara and his spouse Uma.
shots.B13C140S01H02: Narada describes Shiva seated on the Himavat among gods, ghosts and sages, then Uma covering his eyes, the third eye opening and burning the mountain, and Shiva restoring it at her plea.
shots.B13C140S01H03: Uma asks why the third eye appeared, why he burned the mountain, and why he then restored it.
shots.B13C140S01H04: Shiva answers that her covering of his eyes plunged the world into darkness, so he made the third eye to protect creatures, and he later restored Himavat to please her.
shots.B13C140S01H05: Uma asks why his faces differ, why his hair and throat are as they are, why he always holds the Pinaka, and why he is a Brahmacharin, and says she wishes to share his duties.
shots.B13C140S02H01: Narada says Shiva, pleased with Uma, agrees to explain the reasons for his forms.

B13C141.summary: Uma asks Shiva about his four faces, his blue throat, his bull mount and his fondness for the crematorium, and he answers with stories of Tilottama, Indra and Surabhi's kine. She then asks what marks true religion, and Shiva lays out the duties of householders and of each class: Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras. He goes on to describe the householder's path (Pravritti), the path of renunciation (Nivritti) and the kinds of wandering mendicants, and the chapter closes with a survey of ascetic groups such as the Phenapas and Valkhilyas.

scenes.B13C141S01: Shiva explains his four faces, his blue throat, the bull that is his mount, and why the crematorium is a sacred place to him.
scenes.B13C141S02: Uma asks what marks religion, and Shiva names the chief duties of the householder and the five key duties.
scenes.B13C141S03: Uma asks for the duties of each class and of all classes, and Shiva lays out the duties of Brahmanas, householders, kings, Vaisyas and Sudras, then the paths of Pravritti and Nivritti.
scenes.B13C141S04: Uma asks about the religion of the Rishis, and Shiva describes ascetic groups such as the Phenapas and Valkhilyas and the practices of the Munis.

shots.B13C141S01H01: Shiva explains that Tilottama's beauty made him grow four faces to watch her, that each face has its own role, and that Indra's thunderbolt scorched his throat blue.
shots.B13C141S01H02: Uma asks why he has chosen a bull as his mount when many other fine vehicles exist.
shots.B13C141S01H03: Shiva says the bull arose from Surabhi's kine, where a calf's froth angered him, and Brahma gave him the bull as mount and banner device.
shots.B13C141S01H04: Uma asks why he lives in a crematorium, full of bones and carrion, rather than in his heavenly mansions.
shots.B13C141S01H05: Shiva says he finds no spot more sacred than the crematorium, where his ghostly companions gather, and calls it a kind of heaven.
shots.B13C141S02H01: Uma asks what marks religion and how people come to know its details well enough to observe them.
shots.B13C141S02H02: Narada says the sages worshipped the goddess with hymns in reply.
shots.B13C141S02H03: Shiva names the foremost householder virtues, then five chief duties, including avoiding others' spouses, not taking what is not given, and avoiding honey and meat.
shots.B13C141S02H04: Uma asks what the meritorious duties of the four orders are.
shots.B13C141S02H05: Shiva says Brahmanas are gods on earth, that fasting and self-restraint are their duty, and that Vedic study is the source of all piety.
shots.B13C141S03H01: Uma says her doubts are not settled and asks for the duties of each of the four orders in detail.
shots.B13C141S03H02: Shiva sets out the duties of Brahmanas, householders, kings, Vaisyas and Sudras, covering study, household rites, royal justice, trade and service.
shots.B13C141S03H03: Uma asks what duties are common to all the orders.
shots.B13C141S03H04: Shiva describes the three religions of Vedas, Smritis and righteous custom, the six duties of Brahmanas, the marks of a good householder, the path of Pravritti, and the path of Nivritti with its four kinds of mendicants.
shots.B13C141S03H05: Uma asks about the high religion of the Rishis, and says she is drawn to those who live in ascetic retreats.
shots.B13C141S04H01: Shiva describes the Phenapas who live on froth, the Valkhilyas in the sun's disc, the Chakracharas near Soma, other ascetic groups, and the austere practices of the Munis, ending with a call to be friendly to all creatures.
shots.B13C141S04H02: A heading marks the start of Section CXLII.

B13C142.summary: Uma asks Shiva what duties forest recluses follow and what rewards different austerities bring. Shiva describes the daily rites, plain diet, hard postures and bodily hardships of these recluses, and says the married and unmarried kinds differ in their rules but share virtues such as harmlessness and sincerity. He then lists the heavenly and royal rewards for various fasts, vows and deaths, including dying in the manner of heroes.

scenes.B13C142S01: Uma asks about forest recluses, and Shiva describes their rites, austerities and virtues, including harmlessness and sincerity.
scenes.B13C142S02: Shiva lists the rewards that come from different austerities, from heavenly realms to kingship.

shots.B13C142S01H01: Uma asks about the sacred rules followed by forest recluses who depend on themselves alone for protection.
shots.B13C142S01H02: Shiva describes the daily rites, diet, hardships and postures of forest recluses, and says those who follow them reach Brahma's region or Soma's.
shots.B13C142S01H03: Uma asks how the rules differ for recluses who roam freely and for those who keep wives.
shots.B13C142S01H04: Shiva says free and married recluses have different marks, but both should perform rites and avoid harm, and that sincerity is the core of righteousness.
shots.B13C142S01H05: Uma asks which duties bring splendour to ascetics, reward kings and poor men, and lead forest dwellers to an eternal place.
shots.B13C142S02H01: Shiva lists the rewards for fasting, ascetic vows, self-denial and heroic death, which range from heavenly realms to kingship and other regions.

B13C143.summary: Uma asks how people fall from their caste into a lower order and how lower-born men can rise to Brahmanhood. Shiva says birth gives the first order, but conduct decides whether a man keeps or loses it, so a Brahmana who neglects his duties or eats forbidden food sinks to a lower status. He lists the faults that cost a Brahmana his standing, and the good conduct by which Sudras and Vaisyas can rise, and says conduct, not birth alone, makes a Brahmana.

scenes.B13C143S01: Uma asks how castes are lost and gained, and Shiva explains that conduct, not birth alone, decides a man's standing, with lists of faults and of good conduct.

shots.B13C143S01H01: Uma asks how a Vaisya can become a Sudra, how Kshatriyas and Brahmanas can fall in caste, and how such falls can be prevented.
shots.B13C143S01H02: Shiva says birth gives the first order but conduct keeps it, lists the faults that cost a Brahmana his status, sets out the duties by which Sudras and Vaisyas can rise, and says conduct alone makes a Brahmana.

B13C144.summary: Uma asks what deeds, words and thoughts bind men and what frees them, and what lets them reach heaven. Shiva lists righteous conduct, honest wealth, harmlessness, faithfulness to one's spouse, truthful and gentle speech, and good mental habits such as not coveting what belongs to others. Uma then asks what makes life long or short, and Shiva says cruelty brings hell and a short life, while compassion brings long life and a divine state.

scenes.B13C144S01: Uma asks about the deeds, words and thoughts that bind or free men, and Shiva lists the conduct and speech that lead to heaven.
scenes.B13C144S02: Shiva describes the good mental habits that lead to heaven, and then explains how cruelty and compassion shape a person's lifespan and fortune.

shots.B13C144S01H01: Uma asks what conduct and acts take men to heaven, given that thought, word and deed bind them.
shots.B13C144S01H02: Shiva lists conduct that leads to heaven: living righteously, earning wealth honestly, avoiding harm and others' spouses, and restraint in sex.
shots.B13C144S01H03: Uma asks which words bind men and which free them.
shots.B13C144S01H04: Shiva lists speech that leads to heaven, such as avoiding lies, harsh and cruel words, and quarrels, and speaking gently and truthfully.
shots.B13C144S01H05: Uma asks which mental acts or thoughts bind a person.
shots.B13C144S02H01: Shiva describes good thoughts that lead to heaven, such as not coveting others' goods or spouses, friendliness to all, compassion, faith and justice.
shots.B13C144S02H02: Uma asks what acts make a life long or short, and why people differ in fortune, birth, looks, wisdom and suffering.
shots.B13C144S02H03: Shiva says cruelty brings hell and a short life, while those who spare all creatures gain long life and divine status.

B13C145.summary: Uma asks which dispositions and gifts lead a man to heaven. Shiva says generous giving, honouring Brahmanas and the needy, and building wells, halls and tanks win heaven and a rich human birth, while miserliness, arrogance and cruelty lead to hell and humble rebirth. Uma then asks why some people are wise and others foolish, or born blind or diseased, and Shiva ties these to the deeds of learning, lust and cruelty. The chapter closes by contrasting conduct guided by the Vedas with conduct led by folly.

scenes.B13C145S01: Shiva describes the generous giver and the stingy or cruel, with their rewards and punishments, and then answers Uma's questions on wisdom and bodily defects.
scenes.B13C145S02: Shiva explains that those who seek instruction gain wisdom, and that conduct guided by the Vedas differs from conduct led by folly.

shots.B13C145S01H01: Uma asks by what disposition, conduct, acts and gifts a man reaches heaven.
shots.B13C145S01H02: Shiva describes the generous giver who gains heaven and a rich birth, the stingy and arrogant who sink to hell and humble birth, the gentle who gain heaven, and the violent who sink to hell.
shots.B13C145S01H03: Uma asks why some people are wise and others foolish, and why some are born blind, diseased or impotent.
shots.B13C145S01H04: Shiva says learners who seek what is good gain wisdom and heaven, while those who lust after others' wives or harm others suffer blindness, disease or impotence.
shots.B13C145S01H05: Uma asks which acts are faulty and which lead to the highest good.
shots.B13C145S02H01: Shiva says a man who asks Brahmanas about righteousness and follows what is good gains heaven and is born intelligent.
shots.B13C145S02H02: Uma asks why some men hate righteousness, while others keep vows, perform sacrifices or act like Rakshasas.
shots.B13C145S02H03: Shiva says men who follow the Vedas keep their vows, while those led by folly reject them and become the lowest of men, the Brahmarakshasas.

B13C146.summary: Mahadeva asks Uma to set out the duties of women, and she first consults the sacred rivers, led by Ganga, who praises her for asking. Uma then describes the wife's ideal: she should honour her husband as a god, serve him cheerfully, keep the household and its guests and dependants cared for, and share in his merit. The text adds that a wife should comply even with an improper command in a time of distress. The gods and rivers then depart.

scenes.B13C146S01: Mahadeva asks Uma about women's duties, she consults the rivers, and then she sets out the ideal wife's conduct.
scenes.B13C146S02: Mahadeva praises Uma and dismisses the assembly, which departs.

shots.B13C146S01H01: Narada says that after speaking, Mahadeva wanted to listen, so he asked his wife to speak.
shots.B13C146S01H02: Shiva praises Uma's knowledge and virtue, names several goddesses who revered their husbands, and asks her to explain women's duties.
shots.B13C146S01H03: Uma says she will first consult the sacred rivers, and calls them, with Ganga foremost, to her.
shots.B13C146S01H04: Uma says she wants the rivers' opinions first, and Ganga, chosen to answer, praises Uma's learning and encourages her to speak.
shots.B13C146S01H05: Uma describes the wife's duties: devotion to her husband as a god, cheerful service, household rites, care for kin and guests, and sharing in his merit, even when he asks something improper in distress.
shots.B13C146S02H01: Narada says Mahadeva praised Uma and dismissed the assembly, and the spirits, rivers, Gandharvas and Apsaras departed.

B13C147.summary: The Rishis ask Shiva to describe the glory of Vasudeva, and Shiva answers with a long praise of Hari. He calls Vishnu the eternal supreme being, the source of Brahma, Shiva and all creatures, and traces his coming birth through the royal lines of Manu and Yadu. He foretells that Vasudeva will defeat Jarasandha and rule from Dwaraka, and urges all to worship him. He also describes an elder brother, who carries a plough and is identified with the infinite serpent Ananta, and ends by urging the ascetics to worship Krishna.

scenes.B13C147S01: The Rishis ask about Vasudeva, and Shiva praises Hari, traces his future lineage, and urges worship of him.

shots.B13C147S01H01: The Rishis ask Shiva to tell them the glory of Vasudeva.
shots.B13C147S01H02: Shiva praises Hari as the eternal supreme being and source of the gods, then traces his future birth through Manu and Yadu, foretells his victory over Jarasandha and his rule from Dwaraka, and urges all to worship him.

B13C148.summary: After Shiva's discourse, the Rishis see a storm, the ghostly host vanish, and then leave, praising Krishna as Brahma. Krishna returns to Dwaraka, where Rukmini bears him a son. Bhishma then extols Krishna at length, credits him with the Pandavas' victory, and tells Yudhishthira not to grieve, since Time, which is Krishna, has slain the fallen. Yudhishthira stays silent until Bhishma rests, and then he asks a further question.

scenes.B13C148S01: The Rishis describe what they saw and praise Krishna, Bhishma extols Krishna and urges Yudhishthira not to grieve, and Yudhishthira prepares to ask again.

shots.B13C148S01H01: Narada describes the storm and the vanishing of the ghostly host, recalls the burning of Himavat, and says the Rishis took Krishna for the eternal Brahma and recited Shiva's glory to him.
shots.B13C148S01H02: The Rishis praise Krishna, say nothing is hidden from him, take their leave, and wish him a son like himself.
shots.B13C148S01H03: Bhishma says Krishna returned to Dwaraka where Rukmini bore a son, praises him at length as the eternal source who guided the Pandavas, and tells Yudhishthira not to grieve, since Time, which is Krishna, slew the fallen; he also urges worship of Mahadeva and blames Duryodhana and his companions for the ruin of the Kurus.
shots.B13C148S01H04: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira stays silent while Bhishma speaks, the kings and Rishis applaud, and Yudhishthira later asks Bhishma another question.

B13C149.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which god is the sole refuge, which religion is foremost, and which hymn frees a living being from birth and death. Bhishma answers that Vasudeva, the Lord of the universe, is the highest refuge, and recites his thousand names, grouped in sets and explained as the god's attributes. He says that reciting the names daily brings success, protection and prosperity by caste and, in the end, liberation, and he presents the hymn as composed by Vyasa.

scenes.B13C149S01: Yudhishthira asks which god and which hymn bring liberation, and Bhishma answers by reciting the thousand names of Vasudeva and describing the benefits of reciting them.

shots.B13C149S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira, having heard the duties and sacred acts, asks Bhishma another question.
shots.B13C149S01H02: Yudhishthira asks who is the one god and sole refuge, which religion is foremost, and which mantras free a being from the bonds of birth and life.
shots.B13C149S01H03: Bhishma says Vasudeva, the infinite lord, should be praised by reciting his thousand names, and then gives the names in sets with explanatory notes, ending with a salutation.
shots.B13C149S01H04: Bhishma says the reciter gains success by caste, freedom from fear and disease, prosperity, and final liberation, and calls the hymn composed by Vyasa.

B13C150.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for a silent recitation that brings daily merit and success at journeys, new buildings and sacrifices. Bhishma gives the Savitri mantra, said to have been taught by Vyasa and recited by royal sages. He says it should be used with the names of Vishnu, the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Aswins, Rishis and the guardians of the quarters, and promises protection from fire, theft, disease and enemies. The chapter ends with Bhishma offering to answer further questions.

scenes.B13C150S01: Yudhishthira asks for the most effective mantra, and Bhishma gives the Savitri mantra with the list of gods and Rishis to be named and the benefits of reciting them.

shots.B13C150S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for a silent recitation that brings daily merit and success on journeys, at new buildings and at sacrifices, and that is consistent with the Vedas.
shots.B13C150S01H02: Bhishma gives the Savitri mantra, with salutations to Vasishtha, Parasara, Ananta and many gods, and lists the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Aswins and Rishis to be named, along with the protections the recitation brings and the kings who used it.

B13C151.summary: Yudhishthira asks whom people should worship and how they should treat others. Bhishma says Brahmanas deserve honour, since humiliating them humiliates the gods, and he describes their virtues and their role in upholding the world. He says a learned Brahmana is worthier still, but even an unlearned one is a god, just as fire and ghee stay sacred wherever they are, so a Brahmana of wicked conduct still deserves honour.

scenes.B13C151S01: Yudhishthira asks whom to honour, and Bhishma says Brahmanas deserve reverence whatever their learning or conduct.

shots.B13C151S01H01: Yudhishthira asks who deserves worship, whom to bow to, and what conduct is faultless toward different classes.
shots.B13C151S01H02: Bhishma says Brahmanas deserve worship and are the upholders of the world, lists their virtues, and says even an ignorant or wicked Brahmana remains a god, as fire and ghee remain sacred wherever they are.

B13C152.summary: Yudhishthira asks what reward comes from honouring Brahmanas, and Bhishma tells of an old quarrel between the king Arjuna, also called Kartavirya, and the wind god. Kartavirya wins boons from the sage Dattatreya, then grows proud and scorns Brahmanas. The wind god warns him that the Brahmanas can cast him down, and the king asks what a Brahmana is like. The chapter ends with his question.

scenes.B13C152S01: Bhishma tells of King Arjuna's boons from Dattatreya, his scorn for Brahmanas, and the wind god's warning, and ends with Arjuna's question.

shots.B13C152S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what reward and success come from worshipping Brahmanas.
shots.B13C152S01H02: Bhishma tells of King Arjuna, who ruled from Mahishmati and won boons from Dattatreya, including a thousand arms in battle, two at home, and the power to rule righteously; a voice then tells him Brahmanas are superior to Kshatriyas.
shots.B13C152S01H03: Arjuna boasts that he can subdue the Brahmanas, who depend on Kshatriyas, and the wind god warns him to bow to them, or they will strip him of his kingdom.
shots.B13C152S01H04: Arjuna asks the wind god what a Brahmana is like and whether he resembles the wind, water, fire, the sun or the sky.

B13C153.summary: The wind god goes on answering Arjuna's boast that Kshatriyas outrank Brahmanas. He lists the power of Brahmanas: Kasyapa paralysed the Earth, Angiras drank the waters, Gautama cursed Indra, the Brahmanas cursed the ocean and Agni, and Kapila reduced Sagara's sons to ashes. He then argues that Arjuna should honour Brahmanas and reflects on the creation of Brahman, saying Brahman was not born from an egg, and Arjuna remains silent.

scenes.B13C153S01: The wind god lists the feats of Brahmanas as proof of their superiority, and then argues that Brahman was not born from an egg.

shots.B13C153S01H01: The wind god cites the power of Brahmanas, from Kasyapa and Angiras to Gautama, Kapila and Aurva, tells Arjuna to honour Agni and Brahmanas, says Brahman was not born from an egg, and Arjuna falls silent.

B13C154.summary: The wind god tells how the king of Anga wished to give the whole earth to the Brahmanas, and how Kasyapa entered and saved the earth. He then tells of Utathya, whose wife was carried off by Varuna, the lord of waters. Angiras dried up the waters, Utathya made the land barren until Varuna returned the wife, and the wind god asks whether any Kshatriya is greater than Utathya.

scenes.B13C154S01: The wind god tells the stories of Kasyapa and the earth, and of Utathya's wife, to show Brahmanas surpass Kshatriyas, and then asks Arjuna for a reply.

shots.B13C154S01H01: The wind god tells how the Anga king's gift of the earth led Kasyapa to save her, then tells how Varuna took Utathya's wife, how Angiras dried the waters and Utathya made the land barren until she was returned, and asks whether any Kshatriya is greater than Utathya.

B13C155.summary: Bhishma reports that the wind god told Arjuna of two Brahmanas whose powers exceeded any Kshatriya's. Agastya burned the Danavas who had seized the sacrifices, but refused to destroy the Asuras hidden underground, because that would cost him penance. Vasishtha burned the Khalins who had attacked the gods, and brought the Ganga to the spot to protect them. Each time the wind god asks Arjuna whether any Kshatriya can surpass these Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C155S01: The wind god tells of Agastya and Vasishtha, each defeating Danavas or Asuras to save the gods, and asks Arjuna whether any Kshatriya surpasses them.

shots.B13C155S01H01: The wind god tells how Agastya burned the Danavas who had driven the gods from their sacrifices and refused to destroy the Asuras underground, since that would cost him penance, and asks whether any Kshatriya is greater.
shots.B13C155S01H02: Bhishma says Arjuna stays silent, and the wind god tells how Vasishtha burned the Khalins, brought the Ganga to the lake, and saved the gods, and asks whether any Kshatriya surpasses him.

B13C156.summary: The wind god offers two more tales of Brahmanas. Atri takes the forms of the sun and moon to dispel darkness caused by Rahu and to defeat the Asuras who attacked the gods. Chyavana then makes Indra accept the Aswins as Soma drinkers, creating the terrible Mada to threaten him when Indra refuses, and sends Mada to dwell in dice, hunting, drink and women. The wind god again asks whether Arjuna can name a Kshatriya higher than Chyavana.

scenes.B13C156S01: The wind god tells of Atri, who dispelled the darkness caused by Rahu, and of Chyavana, who first asks Indra to let the Aswins drink Soma.
scenes.B13C156S02: Indra refuses, Chyavana threatens him, creates the monster Mada, and Indra submits; Mada is then given his dwelling places.

shots.B13C156S01H01: Bhishma says Arjuna remains silent, and the wind god tells how Rahu struck the sun and moon with arrows in the gods' battle with the Danavas, and how the gods came to Atri for help.
shots.B13C156S01H02: Atri takes the forms of the sun and moon, drives off the darkness, defeats the Asuras, and the wind god asks whether any Kshatriya is greater than this Brahmana.
shots.B13C156S01H03: The wind god tells of Chyavana, who had promised the Aswins that the gods would let them drink Soma, and who asked Indra to do so.
shots.B13C156S01H04: Indra says the Aswins have been cast out and are not counted among the gods, so he will not drink Soma with them.
shots.B13C156S01H05: Chyavana insists the Aswins are gods, being sons of Surya, and warns that disobedience will bring evil on the gods.
shots.B13C156S02H01: Indra says again that he will not drink Soma with the Aswins.
shots.B13C156S02H02: Chyavana vows that Indra will drink Soma with the Aswins that very day, by his compulsion.
shots.B13C156S02H03: The wind god says Chyavana began the rite, Indra attacked with a mountain and thunderbolt, and Chyavana paralysed him, created the monster Mada from his libations, and forced Indra to bow; Mada was then given his roles in dice, hunting, drink and women, and the wind god asks whether Arjuna knows a Kshatriya higher than Chyavana.

B13C157.summary: The wind god tells how Chyavana took the earth from the gods and the Kapas took heaven, so the gods sought Brahman's help. Brahman sent them to the Brahmanas, who burned the Kapas with sacred fires after refusing a messenger's plea, and Narada told the gods that the Brahmanas had won. Arjuna thanks the wind god and credits Dattatreya for his might, and the wind god urges him to protect the Brahmanas and warns of future danger from the race of Bhrigu.

scenes.B13C157S01: The wind god tells how the gods lost heaven and earth, how the Brahmanas destroyed the Kapas, and Arjuna's response.
scenes.B13C157S02: The wind god urges Arjuna to protect the Brahmanas and warns him of future danger from the race of Bhrigu.

shots.B13C157S01H01: Bhishma says Arjuna stays silent, and the wind god tells how Chyavana took the earth from the gods, who had already lost heaven, so they turned to Brahman for protection.
shots.B13C157S01H02: The gods tell Brahman that Chyavana took the earth and the Kapas took heaven.
shots.B13C157S01H03: Brahman sends the gods to the Brahmanas, who agree to subdue the Kapas, even after the messenger Dhanin describes the Kapas' many virtues and urges them to stop.
shots.B13C157S01H04: The Brahmanas refuse, the Kapas attack, and the Brahmanas burn them with sacred fires; Narada tells the gods that the Brahmanas were the victors, and the gods regain strength, and Arjuna worships the wind god.
shots.B13C157S01H05: Arjuna says he lives for the Brahmanas, and that his might comes from Dattatreya's grace.
shots.B13C157S02H01: The wind god urges Arjuna to protect the Brahmanas as a Kshatriya should and warns of future danger from the race of Bhrigu.

B13C158.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma what reward comes from honouring Brahmanas. Bhishma says he is nearing death and that Krishna should answer, and he then praises Krishna at length. He describes Krishna as the source of the earth, the sky and the gods, who takes birth in each age to uphold righteousness and who lifted Govardhana and raised the earth as a boar. He calls Krishna the one called Vishwaksena, in whom the seasons, Vedas, elements and the four forms of Vasudeva are all contained.

scenes.B13C158S01: Yudhishthira asks his question, and Bhishma, near death, refers him to Krishna while praising Krishna as creator, protector and the whole universe.

shots.B13C158S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma what fruit and prosperity come from worshipping Brahmanas.
shots.B13C158S01H02: Bhishma says his faculties are failing and that Krishna should answer, then praises Krishna at length as the creator of all, who appears in every age, lifted Govardhana, and is the many-named Vishwaksena in whom the cosmos is contained.

B13C159.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna what prosperity comes from honouring Brahmanas, and Krishna recounts how his son Pradyumna once put the same question to him. Krishna tells how the sage Durvasa stayed in his house, wrecked his goods, humiliated Rukmini, and then blessed the couple and restored everything he had broken. Krishna concludes that his own prosperity comes from the grace of Brahmanas, and he urges Yudhishthira to honour them daily.

scenes.B13C159S01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna about Brahmanas, and Krishna tells the story of Durvasa's stay in his house and the lesson he drew from it.

shots.B13C159S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to explain the prosperity that comes from honouring Brahmanas.
shots.B13C159S01H02: Krishna tells how Pradyumna asked him the same question, then recounts how the sage Durvasa stayed in his house, wrecked his goods, yoked Rukmini to a car, and then blessed Krishna and Rukmini and restored everything, after which Krishna always honoured Brahmanas.
shots.B13C159S01H03: A heading marks the start of Section CLX.

B13C160.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to explain the knowledge he gained through Durvasa's grace. Krishna recites the Sata-rudriya hymn, which he says Brahman composed, and praises Mahadeva as the highest of beings. He recounts Rudra's fierce deeds, from piercing Daksha's sacrifice to burning the three cities of the Asuras, and then says Durvasa was Mahadeva himself, whose merits cannot be exhausted.

scenes.B13C160S01: Krishna recites the Sata-rudriya praise of Mahadeva, recounts his deeds, and reveals that Durvasa was Mahadeva.

shots.B13C160S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to explain the knowledge he gained through Durvasa's grace and the names of that high-souled one.
shots.B13C160S01H02: Krishna says he recites the Sata-rudriya each morning, praises Mahadeva as supreme, recounts his fierce deeds at Daksha's sacrifice and against the Asuras' three cities, and says Durvasa was Mahadeva himself.

B13C161.summary: Krishna lists the many names of Rudra and explains their meanings, drawing on his greatness, his wrath, his care for creatures and his acts. He says Rudra has a fierce form and a mild form, and that he dwells in crematoria, gives and takes away life, and is the Lord of all. Brahmanas are said to recite the Sata-rudriya in his honour.

scenes.B13C161S01: Krishna names Rudra and explains the meaning of his names, his two forms, and the worship owed to him.

shots.B13C161S01H01: Krishna names Mahadeva and his forms, explains the sense of names such as Maheswara, Rudra, Mahadeva, Sthanu, Pasupati and Iswara, and says Brahmanas recite the Sata-rudriya in his honour.

B13C162.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether direct perception or scripture is the true authority. Bhishma says that claiming perception alone is authoritative is foolish, that Brahman is understood only through long study and yoga, and that Righteousness is one though seen through three supports: the Vedas, observed practice and purity of conduct. He lists the virtues of the righteous, sets out the fates of those who love or hate Righteousness, and gives a long set of rules on conduct, purity and confession of sin.

scenes.B13C162S01: Yudhishthira asks which source of knowledge is authoritative, and Bhishma says reasoning alone cannot settle it and that Righteousness rests on three supports, which Yudhishthira then questions.
scenes.B13C162S02: Bhishma says Righteousness is one, lists its basic virtues, describes the fates of those who love or hate it, and gives many rules for the good man's conduct.

shots.B13C162S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which is the authority for a conclusion, direct perception or scripture.
shots.B13C162S01H02: Bhishma says doubts are easy to raise and hard to settle, and calls it foolish to say that only perception is authoritative, since Brahman is understood only through long study and yoga.
shots.B13C162S01H03: Yudhishthira asks which of four sources is most authoritative: perception, inference, scripture, or the practice of the good.
shots.B13C162S01H04: Bhishma says Righteousness is attacked by wicked men and can be obscured, so doubts attach to perception, inference and good conduct, and the wise should be consulted.
shots.B13C162S01H05: Yudhishthira says his understanding is confused, since if the three are authorities then Righteousness seems to be of three kinds.
shots.B13C162S02H01: Bhishma says Righteousness is one though seen from three points, tells Yudhishthira to follow the rules without wrangling, and names harmlessness, truth, forgiveness and liberality as its foundations, along with honour to Brahmanas.
shots.B13C162S02H02: Yudhishthira asks what becomes of those who hate Righteousness and of those who uphold it.
shots.B13C162S02H03: Bhishma says haters of Righteousness go to hell, while those who honour it reach heaven, and he calls Brahmanas, the eldest sons of Brahman, its embodiment.
shots.B13C162S02H04: Yudhishthira asks how the wicked and the good can be recognised.
shots.B13C162S02H05: Bhishma lists the marks of the good: courteous conduct, honour to elders and Brahmanas, rules on food, speech and sex, and confession of sins, which is said to be needed before sin can be destroyed.

B13C163.summary: Yudhishthira asks why effort and luck seem to fall unevenly, so that the fortunate prosper and the learned sometimes do not. Bhishma replies that when fortune fails, one should practise austerity and generosity, which bring rewards in later lives, and that a life free from cruelty brings long life. He ends by urging Yudhishthira to be tranquil, since the fates of even insects and ants follow their acts and nature.

scenes.B13C163S01: Yudhishthira asks why wealth and success do not follow effort or learning, and Bhishma answers that austerity, generosity and harmlessness are the way to better fortune in later lives.

shots.B13C163S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why wealth and success seem to fall to the fortunate and not to the hardworking or learned, since some fools prosper and some learned men fail.
shots.B13C163S01H02: Bhishma says that if effort fails, one should practise austerity, make gifts, avoid cruelty and be gentle, and that all creatures' fates follow their acts and nature, so Yudhishthira should be tranquil.

B13C164.summary: Bhishma says that Time moves creatures towards righteousness or sin, and that a righteous soul stays pure, since sin cannot overcome Righteousness, which is eternal. He explains that the four orders share the same elements but have different duties, and that heaven as a reward is temporary while Righteousness is not. He ends by saying that unequal lots among men follow from their past acts.

scenes.B13C164S01: Bhishma explains that Time moves creatures, that Righteousness keeps the soul pure and is eternal, and that the unequal lots of men follow their past acts.

shots.B13C164S01H01: Bhishma says Time moves creatures toward good or evil, Righteousness keeps the soul pure and cannot be overcome by sin, the four orders share one substance but different duties, heavenly rewards pass but Righteousness does not, and inequalities among men come from past acts.

B13C165.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, what brings happiness and cleanses sins. Bhishma recites a long list of gods, sages, sacred waters and mountains, Rishis of each quarter, and kings, and says that naming them morning, noon and evening cleanses a person of sin. He ends with a prayer that these lords will bring growth, long life and victory.

scenes.B13C165S01: Yudhishthira asks what cleanses sin, and Bhishma recites the names of gods, sacred places, Rishis and kings, with the benefits of reciting them.

shots.B13C165S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira asks Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, a question about sin.
shots.B13C165S01H02: Yudhishthira asks what helps a person in this world, what brings happiness, and what destroys sin.
shots.B13C165S01H03: Vaisampayana says Bhishma recites the names of the deities to Yudhishthira, who wants to hear them.
shots.B13C165S01H04: Bhishma says naming the gods, Rishis, sacred rivers and mountains, and kings morning, noon and evening cleanses sins, and closes with a prayer for growth, long life and victory.

B13C166.summary: Janamejaya asks what Yudhishthira did after hearing Bhishma's teachings. Vaisampayana says that Vyasa tells Bhishma that Yudhishthira is ready to leave, and Bhishma sends him back to the city. Bhishma urges him to rule well, honour the gods and gladden his subjects, and to return when Bhishma's departure is near, at the sun's turn north.

scenes.B13C166S01: Janamejaya asks what Yudhishthira did next, and Vaisampayana tells how Bhishma sends the king home with advice and a summons to return.

shots.B13C166S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what Yudhishthira did after hearing Bhishma's teachings and having his doubts resolved.
shots.B13C166S01H02: Vaisampayana says Vyasa tells Bhishma that Yudhishthira is ready to leave, and Bhishma sends him back to the city with advice to rule well and a summons to return when the sun turns north, and Yudhishthira agrees and goes to the city named after the elephant.

B13C167.summary: Yudhishthira rules his kingdom and, after fifty nights, returns to Bhishma with funeral materials, finding him still on the bed of arrows. Bhishma notes that the sun has begun its northward course and that Magha has come, consoles Dhritarashtra, and praises Krishna as the eternal soul. Krishna grants leave to depart, and Bhishma bids his kin farewell, urging them to seek truth and honour Brahmanas, preceptors and priests.

scenes.B13C167S01: Yudhishthira returns to Bhishma with the funeral materials, Bhishma speaks to him, to Dhritarashtra and to Krishna, and asks leave to die.
scenes.B13C167S02: Krishna grants leave, and Bhishma bids farewell to his kin and advises Yudhishthira on honouring Brahmanas.

shots.B13C167S01H01: Yudhishthira consoles the widows, recovers his kingdom, is installed on the throne, and after fifty nights sets out with funeral materials to find Bhishma still on his bed, surrounded by sages and kings.
shots.B13C167S01H02: Bhishma greets Yudhishthira, says the sun has begun its northward course and Magha has come, and says he has lain on the arrows for fifty-eight nights.
shots.B13C167S01H03: Bhishma tells Dhritarashtra not to grieve, since what was fated has happened, and asks him to cherish the Pandavas, whom he calls his sons in moral terms.
shots.B13C167S01H04: Vaisampayana says Bhishma then turns to Vasudeva.
shots.B13C167S01H05: Bhishma praises Krishna as the supreme soul and asks leave to depart, recalling that he urged Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas and that Duryodhana refused.
shots.B13C167S02H01: Vasudeva grants Bhishma leave and says he will attain the status of the Vasus, comparing him to Markandeya.
shots.B13C167S02H02: Bhishma bids his friends and kin farewell, urges them to seek truth and keep company with righteous Brahmanas, and asks Yudhishthira to honour Brahmanas, priests and preceptors.

B13C168.summary: Chapter 168 is the translator's footnote section that follows the Anushasana Parva. Its only narrative scene, S01, closes the Parva with Bhishma's death and funeral, Ganga's lament and Krishna's consolation. The numbered footnotes that follow, running to 631, gloss Sanskrit words, identify plants and animals, correct readings, criticise earlier translations and comment on gifts, marriage, rites and duties.

scenes.B13C168S01: Bhishma's life-breaths leave his body through his head, his funeral is held, and Ganga, lamenting her son, is consoled by Krishna and Vyasa.
scenes.B13C168S02: The translator's footnotes 2 to 6 gloss a simile about fire, a curse on Viswamitra, and two star names.
scenes.B13C168S03: Footnotes 7 to 11 explain Matanga's birth, the term charu, and a sentence about destiny, exertion and the swan image.
scenes.B13C168S04: Footnotes 12 to 16 gloss a few terms about energy, penance, and the expectation of a Brahmana.
scenes.B13C168S05: Footnotes 17 to 21 explain a physician simile, terms for peace and asceticism, and renunciation.
scenes.B13C168S06: Footnotes 22 to 26 cover the rule against Brahmanas serving Sudras at rites, the Atharva Veda, and the punyaha and diksha rites.
scenes.B13C168S07: Footnotes 27 to 31 gloss barter, hypocrisy, offerings, childlessness and three mental acts.
scenes.B13C168S08: Footnotes 32 to 36 discuss Vasudeva's favour from Mahadeva and the sons Krishna won by penance.
scenes.B13C168S09: Footnotes 37 onward give botanical identities for a set of trees, Dhava, Kakubha, Arjuna, Kadamva, Kuruveka, Ketaka, Jamvu and Patala.
scenes.B13C168S10: A continuation of the tree-name footnotes: Varunaka, Vatasanabha, Vilwa, Sarala, Kapittha, Piyala, Sala, Vadari and Kunda.
scenes.B13C168S11: The tree-name footnotes end with Punnaga, Asoka, Amra, Kovidara, Champaka and Panasa, followed by footnote 38 on Ganga as Jahnavi.
scenes.B13C168S12: Footnotes 39 to 43 explain ascetics who do not use their hands, the word graha, the term yoga, Surabhi, and the sanyasin and king.
scenes.B13C168S13: Footnotes 44 to 48 explain the sacred thread, arupa, the sheaths of the soul, and devotion to Mahadeva.
scenes.B13C168S14: Footnotes 49 and 50 explain how Mahadeva cannot be grasped without the Srutis and how he filled Space and set the egg of Brahma.
scenes.B13C168S15: Footnotes 54 to 58 discuss a difficult verse on Mahadeva's compassion, the seed that turned into a golden mountain, and the Haragauri form.
scenes.B13C168S16: Footnotes 59 to 63 weigh variant readings of verses on Mahadeva's form and on sacrifice that goes beyond action.
scenes.B13C168S17: Footnotes 64 to 68 comment on a disputed name, the sense of Vishnu, gifts to a visitor, a genitive form, and a cloud image.
scenes.B13C168S18: Footnotes 69 to 73 gloss terms for action and its fruit, the powers of Yoga, and the link between acts and time.
scenes.B13C168S19: Footnotes 74 to 78 comment on variant readings, the sixteen boons of Upamanyu, Ganga's cleansing power, and the six divisions of the self and world.
scenes.B13C168S20: Footnotes 79 to 83 explain how the liberated behold Mahadeva in their hearts, the cave of Brahman, and his eight forms.
scenes.B13C168S21: Footnotes 84 to 88 explain the two paths of the departed, the three ways of worship, a Sankhya reference, a difficult verse, and the protective power of the names.
scenes.B13C168S22: Footnotes 89 to 93 explain the merit of the names, the sense of sthira and sthanu, bhava, Virat, and the many senses of certain names.
scenes.B13C168S23: Footnotes 94 to 98 explain names for the displayed universe, the inner soul, niyama, nidhi and the many-eyed.
scenes.B13C168S24: Footnotes 99 to 103 explain astronomical names, the golden seed, the soul's seed of acts, and Ganesa.
scenes.B13C168S25: Footnotes 104 to 108 explain knowledge as penance, a weapon named sataghni, the name Harikesa, Krishna, and Kaparddin.
scenes.B13C168S26: Footnotes 109 to 113 explain space as Mahadeva's abode, the deities and Asuras, unmanifest sound, four states of the soul, and Buddha.
scenes.B13C168S27: Footnotes 114 to 118 explain Mahadeva's contest with Krishna, the vision of Markandeya, and the three names as householder, sanyasin and recluse.
scenes.B13C168S28: Footnotes 119 to 123 gloss Brahman within the heart, Yama's covering illusion, the terms vibhaga and sarvaga, and the golden mail of illusion.
scenes.B13C168S29: Footnotes 124 to 128 gloss Pasupati, the waves of worldly joy, the binder of Asura chiefs, the ritual of sacrifice, and the question of vestments.
